articles.title: Inside Kritika Kamra’s Mumbai home: Actor calls serene rental apartment ‘house of my 30s’  that blends Indian textiles, chanderi craftsmanship, vintage furniture and modern decor
articles.summary: Kritika Kamra’s Mumbai rental apartment is a reflection of her personality, aesthetic sensibilities and deep appreciation for Indian textiles and craf.
articles.body: Kritika Kamra’s Mumbai rental apartment is a reflection of her personality, aesthetic sensibilities and deep appreciation for Indian textiles and craftsmanship. Designed as a warm and serene retreat away from the demands of her profession, the home combines muted neutrals, vintage-inspired furniture, colourful textiles and contemporary accents. With interiors that blend Indian artisanship with a modern, global sensibility, Kritika has transformed her rental apartment into a cosy oasis that also doubles as a stylish space for entertaining and creating digital content.Kritika Kamra wanted her Mumbai home to feel like a ‘homely oasis’Unlike many celebrity homes that prominently display film posters, photographs and memorabilia, Kritika deliberately chose a different approach for her Mumbai apartment. The actor wanted the space to feel removed from her professional life and instead serve as a peaceful retreat.“I may be an actor, but I didn’t want my posters and pictures splayed across the walls…I don’t even have a dresser with lights. I spend so much time in trailers that I needed this house to be my homely oasis. You won’t see the actor side of me here,” Kritika shared.The apartment had already been spacious, well-lit and conveniently located for her shoots and work commitments. Rather than moving into another home, Kritika wanted to refresh the existing space and make it feel more personal.“This is not my family home—my parents don't live with me—and I know this is not a permanent house. For me, this is the house of my 30s. And that's what I told Purva—I want this to be the house of my 30s,” she said.“I realised this place was spacious enough for me. It gets great light, it’s on a higher floor, and very conveniently located for all my shoots and offices. I didn't want to move out of the house, but I wanted it to feel new—more like a home.”Indian textiles bring warmth and character to the living room at Kritika Kamra's homeThe living room follows a beige and white colour palette, creating a calm and balanced atmosphere. Vintage-style furniture, a gold-framed console, textured artwork and a multicoloured rug add layers without making the space feel overly decorated.One of the most distinctive elements is a grid wall showcasing textiles from Cinnabar, the handloom label founded by Kritika during the lockdown. The Chanderi textiles were hand-dyed to complement the room’s muted colour scheme, bringing Indian craftsmanship into the contemporary interiors.The apartment continues this blend of traditional textiles and modern design through pastel furnishings, blush-pink velvet seating, muted blue bone-inlay side tables, floral pouffes and a gold-framed coffee table. The combination gives the room a feminine yet eclectic character while maintaining the relaxed quality Kritika wanted.A cosy dining nook adds a European-inspired charmThe dining area introduces a softer, more intimate character to the apartment. Pastel blue walls are paired with neutral furniture, including an ivory bench, a custom fluted-marble round dining table and rattan-upholstered chairs.A vintage Art Deco pink marble pendant light becomes a standout feature, while ikat wallpaper and artwork visually separate the dining nook from the rest of the living space.The overall aesthetic brings together the warmth of Indian textiles with the understated elegance of European-inspired interiors, creating a space that works equally well for everyday meals and intimate gatherings.Kritika Kamra’s home also has a dedicated coffee cornerAn existing window between the kitchen and dining area was expanded to create a more open connection between the two spaces. A subtle arch further softens the transition and creates a dedicated corner for morning coffee. Custom red and orange bar chairs add a striking pop of colour against the otherwise muted palette, while a bar cabinet provides additional storage for glassware and helps make the space functional as well as visually appealing.Guest bedroom designed as a minimalist sanctuaryThe guest bedroom maintains the apartment’s soothing aesthetic with a mint-blue wall and muted blue and green bedding. A geometric artwork adds visual interest while keeping the room uncluttered. The space continues the larger design philosophy of the apartment—minimalism balanced with colour, texture and carefully selected statement pieces.Media room brings a vibrant contrast to the homeThe media room is more playful and energetic than the rest of the apartment. An eclectic collection wall of art prints is paired with chequered and geometric patterns, creating a vibrant multifunctional space. The room also gives Kritika another setting for creating content for her digital platforms, one of the practical requirements behind the redesign of her home.Kritika Kamra wanted a home that reflected her personalityFor Kritika, the makeover was not about following a conventional celebrity-home aesthetic. Instead, she wanted the apartment to evolve with her and reflect where she was in her life. The home combines Indian textiles, vintage details, contemporary furniture and muted colours while maintaining enough visual variety to create different backdrops for her personal and professional needs.“I want this to be the house of my 30s,” Kritika’s vision captures the larger philosophy behind the makeover—a home that feels personal, lived-in and distinctly separate from her identity as an actor.Kritika Kamra and Gaurav Kapur’s home wedding and new chapterEarlier in March, Kritika Kamra and Gaurav Kapur reportedly began preparing their Bandra residence for their wedding celebrations, with the couple opting to redesign key areas of the home ahead of their intimate ceremony. Their vision reportedly focused on blending traditional and mid-century modern elements, along with plants, natural light and a warm, airy atmosphere. The renovation focused on spaces including the living room, dining area, kitchen and bedroom, creating a welcoming setting for family and friends, as reported by us (TNN) in March.The couple tied the knot on March 11, 2026, in an intimate, low-key wedding. The couple opted for a cozy home wedding, holding a sundowner ceremony on the terrace of their Bandra residence in Mumbai surrounded by close family and friends. Kritika wore a traditional red saree, while Gaurav opted for a classic custom bandhgala. The intimate ceremony was followed by a reception hosted for close friends from both the film industry and the cricket fraternity. articles.title: 2026 Emmy Awards: How to watch, time, channel, host, nominations and more
articles.summary: Hollywood’s biggest night in television is back after a year of new beginnings. The 2026 Emmys will take place Monday, Sept. 14, at 8 p.m. ET.
articles.body: The Primetime Emmy Awards, Hollywood’s biggest night in television, is back after a year of new beginnings and heartfelt endings. Several shows in their first seasons have garnered multiple nods, with “Widow’s Bay” up for 19 awards, “Pluribus” 18, “DTF St. Louis” 13, “Spider-Noir” 11 and “The Beast in Me” nine. “The Pitt” leads the overall pack with 25 nominations, followed closely by the final season of “Hacks,” with 24. Fan-favorite “The Late Show with Stephen Colbert” has nine nominations. CBS announced the end of the franchise last year, and the final episode aired in May. Many other familiar shows are back this year, too, including “Beef,” with 16 nominations; “Shrinking,” with 10; “Slow Horses,” with nine; “The Bear,” with eight; “Abbott Elementary,” with seven; and “Only Murders in the Building,” with five. Whether you plan to tune in live or track the winners online, here’s what to expect from this year’s Emmys. When are the 2026 Emmy Awards? The Emmys will take place starting at 8 p.m. ET Monday at the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles. Where can I watch or stream the Emmys? Viewers can watch the broadcast on NBC or stream the event live online with a Peacock subscription. Who is hosting the Emmys in 2026? “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” star Mariska Hargitay will host this year’s Emmys. Hargitay is coming off two wins this season for the documentary “My Mom Jayne.” Hargitay follows 2025 host Nate Bargatze, who made a splash with charity donations for too-long speeches — a stunt with major returns for the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and mixed reviews from audiences for its execution. When does the red carpet start? E! will host red-carpet events throughout the night, with a preshow starting at 5 p.m. Live red-carpet coverage will kick off at 6 p.m. — but fans should expect a blue carpet, instead. Apple TV+ trails with 19 for the first season of “Widow’s Bay” and 18 for Season 1 of “Pluribus.” Who is predicted to win in 2026? This year’s Emmys pit longtime favorites against breakout stars, and shake-ups can be expected. “The Pitt” is likely to take home a decent amount of hardware, and “Widow’s Bay” is poised to make a splash in its first year. Jean Smart is looking for her fifth win in a row for the role of Deborah Vance in “Hacks,” another Emmys favorite. The win would be her eighth, tying her with Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Cloris Leachman for most acting Emmys for a single performer. It won best talk series to raucous applause last year, just months after its fate was announced. Longtime Emmys darling “The Bear” has already earned its first win for best guest actor in a comedy, which went posthumously to Rob Reiner.

articles.title: ‘Practical Magic 2’ conjures a No. 1 box office debut with $30 million
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — “Practical Magic 2” conjured a box-office victory this weekend, opening atop the North American charts nearly three decades after its predecessor grew from a modest theatrical performer into a cult favorite.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — “Practical Magic 2” conjured a box-office victory this weekend, opening atop the North American charts nearly three decades after its predecessor grew from a modest theatrical performer into a cult favorite. The Warner Bros. sequel starring Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman earned an estimated $30 million from 4,146 theaters, according to estimates Sunday from Rentrak. The film knocked “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” out of the top spot after the superhero blockbuster led the domestic box office for six consecutive weekends. “Practical Magic 2” added about $16 million from 77 international markets, giving it a worldwide opening of approximately $46 million. The debut landed at the low end of Warner Bros.’ projected range of $30 million to $35 million. The Susanne Bier-directed film carries a reported $75 million production budget. “It’s the kind of movie that you can build an evening at the movie theater around with your friends,” said Paul Dergarabedian, the senior media analyst for Rentrak. Dergarabedian said the return of Bullock and Kidman was crucial to rekindling interest after such a long gap between films. He said the bigger test will come next weekend, when the sequel faces little direct competition. “It’s not necessarily about that opening weekend,” he said. “Weekend two will tell the tale, no question about it.” “Practical Magic 2” reunites Bullock and Kidman as sisters Sally and Gillian Owens, members of a family of witches whose love lives have long been haunted by an ancestral curse. The sequel finds them trying to end the curse for good and introduces a younger generation of the Owens family, played by Joey King and Maisie Williams. Lee Pace also joins the cast. The film is adapted from the work of author Alice Hoffman and arrives 28 years after the original “Practical Magic.” The 1998 film topped out at $46 million during its initial domestic run but gradually developed a devoted following through home viewing, streaming services and social media. The latest film received two out of four stars from The Associated Press, whose review said the sequel abandons some of the campy fun that helped the original find an unlikely second life, but is buoyed by the strong performances and chemistry of Bullock and Kidman. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” slipped to second with $8.4 million, a 54% drop from the previous weekend. The Sony and Marvel blockbuster starring Tom Holland has now collected roughly $935.2 million domestically. That puts the film within about $1.4 million of the $936.6 million North American total for 2015’s “Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens” and the top spot on the all-time domestic chart. “Think about this movie opening at the end of July, and here we are in the middle of September,” Dergarabedian said. He expects Sony to keep the film in theaters as it pursues an unprecedented $1 billion in unadjusted domestic ticket sales. Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” followed in third with $7.4 million during its ninth weekend. The Universal Pictures mythic epic, starring Matt Damon as Odysseus, has crossed $600.5 million domestically and $1.68 billion worldwide. The movie also passed 2015’s “Jurassic World” to become Universal’s highest-grossing global release. It has also collected a record $506 million from IMAX screens worldwide, accounting for 30% of its global total. Dergarabedian said the staying power of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey,” which both opened in July, demonstrates the range of films moviegoers are willing to embrace. “People aren’t just looking at the movie theater as the home for the traditional cookie-cutter blockbuster,” he said. “They’re looking at the movie theater like they do almost as a streaming service, where there’s this incredible array and mix of genres, stars and types of films.” “Runner” opened in fourth place with $6.6 million. The Angel Studios action-comedy stars Alan Ritchson as a former soldier who joins forces with an unlikely partner, played by Owen Wilson, to complete an organ delivery while being pursued by a ruthless cartel. Directed by Scott Waugh, “Runner” opened in more than 2,500 North American theaters. Ketchup Entertainment’s “Coyote vs. Acme” rounded out the top five, collecting $6.2 million in its third weekend. The live-action and animated Looney Tunes feature has now earned about $47.8 million domestically. In sixth place, “Buddy” brought in $3.5 million during its third weekend, pushing its North American total to $21.3 million. Sony’s “Insidious: Out of the Further” followed in seventh with $3.35 million. The latest installment in the long-running horror franchise has generated roughly $60.5 million domestically and $155.2 million worldwide after four weekends. The South Korean science-fiction thriller “Hope” opened in eighth with $3.3 million from 1,560 locations. Directed by Na Hong-jin, the monster epic stars Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung and Hoyeon and centers on a remote village thrown into chaos by the arrival of a mysterious creature. “The Uprising,” directed by Paul Greengrass and starring Andrew Garfield, debuted in ninth with $3.25 million. The Focus Features historical action drama follows an uprising of commoners against the tyranny of King Richard II in medieval England. “By Any Means” finished 10th with $2.5 million in its second weekend. Domestic box-office revenue for the year stands at $7.5 billion, up 19.2% from the same point in 2025. “What a great summer, a record-breaking summer and a solid start to the fall,” Dergarabedian said. “It’s not like we had a blockbuster debut like we did last year with ‘Demon Slayer,’ but a solid start to a fall movie season that I think will deliver for sure.” Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “Practical Magic 2,” $30 million. 2. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” $8.4 million. 3. “The Odyssey,” $7.4 million. 4. “Runner,” $6.6 million. 5. “Coyote vs. Acme,” $6.2 million. 6. “Buddy,” $3.5 million. 7. “Insidious: Out of the Further,” $3.35 million. 8. “Hope,” $3.3 million. 9. “The Uprising,” $3.25 million. 10. “By Any Means,” $2.5 million.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere: sale a la luz la causa de la muerte
articles.summary: La actriz estadounidense Hayden Panettiere, conocida por sus papeles en la saga de cine de terror 'Scream', falleció tras consumir oxicodona, un analgésico opioide, adulterada con fentanilo, según informa el medio TMZ.
articles.body: La actriz estadounidense Hayden Panettiere, conocida por sus papeles en la saga de cine de terror 'Scream', falleció tras consumir oxicodona, un analgésico opioide, adulterada con fentanilo, según informa el medio TMZ. Hayden Panettiere ingirió una pastilla mortal el día que falleció y, según varias fuentes policiales consultadas por el medio, creen que se trataba de oxicodona adulterada con fentanilo. TMZ asegura que sus fuentes están todas vinculadas al caso y con conocimiento directo y subraya que Hayden tenía un "traficante de drogas" desde hacía tiempo en Los Ángeles, quien le suministraba varios medicamentos procedentes del mercado negro, incluida la oxicodona. "Nos informan de que Hayden consumió varias drogas compradas a su traficante durante el vuelo de Los Ángeles a Carolina del Sur, el día anterior a su muerte", señala el medio especializado en noticias de sociedad. La Administración de Control de Drogas (DEA por sus siglas en inglés) en Los Ángeles está reconstruyendo la relación entre Hayden y su traficante, intentando rastrear el origen de la pastilla mortal. La también modelo y cantante, que falleció a los 36 años el pasado mes de agosto, comenzó su carrera como estrella infantil y desarrolló una larga trayectoria en televisión y cine. Es recordada por su papel como Claire Bennet en la exitosa serie 'Heroes', pero sobre todo, como Juliette Barnes en el drama musical 'Nashville', por el que recibió dos nominaciones a los Globos de Oro. Una serie que protagonizó durante 128 episodios entre 2012 y 2018. También protagonizó 'Remember the Titans' ('Duelo de Titanes'), 'Raising Helen' ('Educando a Helen' o 'Mamá a la fuerza'), 'Ice Princess' ('Sueños sobre hielo' o 'Soñando, soñando... triunfé patinando') y 'Scream 4'. Panettiere habló abiertamente sobre sus dificultades personales desde su infancia hasta la edad adulta en sus memorias tituladas 'This Is Me: A Reckoning' y publicadas en mayo. La actriz fue encontrada en parada cardiorespiratoria cuando los servicios de emergencia llegaron a una residencia, ubicada en los complejos residenciales Judson Mill Lofts en Greenville, Carolina del Sur, tras recibir una llamada de socorro. La autopsia preliminar realizada a la fallecida descartó indicios de violencia.

articles.title: Disappointed air show fans offered free Thruxton race entry
articles.summary: Thruxton Race Circuit offers free entry to ticketholders of the cancelled Hampshire Air Festival.
articles.body:
Ticketholders of an air show that was cancelled less than a week before it was due to take place are being offered free motor racing tickets by the host venue.

Montserrat Events was due to host Hampshire Air Festival at Thruxton aerodrome and race circuit on 12 and 13 September but, on Monday 7 September, organisers said the company would be put into liquidation.

Thruxton Race Circuit said it was not the organiser of the air show but still wanted to welcome people to the venue.

It said anyone with a ticket to the air festival could fill in an online form to claim free entry to any 2027 racing event.

A statement from the circuit, posted on social media, said: "We know a lot of people were looking forward to visiting Thruxton this weekend for the Hampshire Air Festival.

"The event was organised and promoted by Montserrat Events, not by Thruxton Circuit, but it was our venue ticket holders were expecting to visit, and we'd still like the opportunity to welcome you here and give you a great day out.

"So, we'd like to offer every Hampshire Air Festival ticketholder a complimentary admission ticket to a Thruxton race meeting in 2027.

"It won't replace the event you were expecting this weekend, but hopefully it gives something to look forward to and the chance to come and experience Thruxton."

Montserrat Events, which previously organised the Victory Festival and Air Display at Lee-on-the-Solent, said it was with "profound sadness" that it announced the cancellation.

Ticketholders have been advised to contact their card provider to recover their payment.
